text:
If you're trying to salvage an outdoor afternoon, Burlington has mostly cooperated so far. It's 75 under a thick cloud deck, with light wind and no meaningful rain showing up here yet. A stray shower is still possible, but the forecasters' low-end call looks like the better bet over the wetter computer model. Expect more clouds through the evening, with only a small shower chance before midnight. The lake is relatively manageable, with waves around 1 to 2 feet, though conditions turn rougher after dark. Air quality is moderate from particle pollution, so sensitive folks may want to take it easy.

Wednesday stays gray and mild, near 74, but the wind picks up from the south with gusts near 24 mph. Showers arrive late, then heavier rain and a few thunderstorms take over Wednesday night. Enjoy the outdoor window through sunset at 7:29, but don't plan a long evening on the water.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Hopefully you were able to get out and about and enjoy yesterday, as clouds and a few showers are back in play through the day ahead. The rain starts off in the Adirondacks and North Country this morning, gradually sliding south through central and southern Vermont during the day. While northern Vermont does stay mainly dry, they’ll hang onto clouds through the vast majority of the day. Highs range from the mid 60s to mid 70s, with cooler temperatures in the areas that see more showers. We’ll keep the clouds around Tuesday night with the chance for showers, mainly early in the night. Lows will be in the lower 50s.
